q: 1. The discolouration and formation of white deposits due to presence of relatively large proportion of soluble salts in a bricks is known as
explain: Efflorescence is the white powdery deposit left on a brick surface when moisture evaporates and leaves behind soluble salts.

q: 2. Dolomite bricks are
explain: Dolomite is a basic material; therefore, bricks made from it are classified as basic refractory bricks.

q: 3. Jhumb bricks
explain: Jhumb bricks (or Jhama bricks) are over-burnt bricks that have become vitrified and often distorted in shape.

q: 4. The reason for the popularity of bricks as construction material is that
options: they are cheap and available locally at all places
they are durable and possess fairly good strength and lighter than stones
they have very good insulating property against heat and sound
explain: Bricks are widely used due to their cost-effectiveness, durability, ease of handling, and natural insulation properties.

q: 5. The most widely used kiln in Nepal is
explain: Bull's Trench Kiln is the most popular type in Nepal due to its cost-efficiency and ability to produce a large volume of bricks continuously.

q: 6. The standard size of brick as per Indian standard is
explain: The standard modular brick size as per IS: 1077 is 19 cm x 9 cm x 9 cm.

q: 7. The soil used for the manufacture of bricks should preferably not contain the following material
explain: Alkalies cause efflorescence, while pebbles and kankar lead to cracking and weakness in the finished brick.

q: 8. Which of the following ingredients of brick earth enables the brick to retain its shape?
explain: Silica provides the structural bulk and rigidity that helps the brick retain its shape after molding and firing.

q: 9. Bloating of bricks is due to .....
options: presence of excess carbonaceous matter in the clay
presence of gas forming material in the clay
explain: Bloating is caused by gases trapped in the brick, from carbonaceous matter, gas-forming materials or rapid burning.

q: 10. Advantage of a clamp compared to a kiln for burning bricks is that
options: it takes less time for burning
it gives more output of first class bricks
it is suitable when bricks are required in large numbers
explain: A clamp requires far less capital investment to set up compared to a permanent kiln structure.

q: 11. Swelling of bricks is known as .....
explain: The swelling of bricks during burning is called bloating.

q: 12. Efflorescence is caused if
options: the alkaline salt is present in the bricks
the clay used for making bricks contain pyrite
the water used for pugging the clay contains gypsum
explain: Efflorescence can arise from multiple sources of soluble salts — alkalies in the clay, pyrite, or gypsum-contaminated water — all of which crystallize on the surface.

q: 13. To which category do the chromite bricks belong?
explain: Chromite bricks are neutral refractory bricks, and so are bricks of bauxite and carbon.

q: 14. The frog of a brick is normally made on its
explain: The frog is pressed into the top (frog) face of the brick during molding, which also helps key it to the mortar above.

q: 15. The maximum percentages of warping along the sides of tiles, is
explain: Quality control standards for tiles generally allow for a maximum of 2% warping along the edges.

q: 16. The thermal conductivity of glass is
explain: Glass has low thermal conductivity, making it a relatively poor conductor of heat.

q: 17. The frog of a brick is normally made on its .....
explain: As per the answer key, the frog is made on the top face.

q: 18. The internal size of mould used in brick preparation is
options: equal to the size of a fully burnt brick
smaller than the size of a fully burnt brick
greater than the size of a fully burnt brick
explain: The mould is made larger than the final brick size to account for shrinkage that occurs during drying and burning.

q: 19. The strength of a brick decreases by about ........ percent when soaked in water
explain: Water absorption weakens the internal bond structure of a brick, reducing its strength by about 25% when soaked.

q: 20. If the water absorption of bricks is 5% of its weight, the brick may be
explain: A very low water absorption of 5% indicates a dense, high-quality brick, typical of heavy duty machine-made bricks.

q: 21. The colour of fire bricks is generally
explain: Fire bricks, made from fire clay low in iron oxide, typically fire to a yellowish-white color.

q: 22. Efflorescence in bricks is caused by
options: the high pH content of water used during pugging
low silica content of the bricks
explain: Efflorescence results from soluble alkaline salts within the brick migrating to the surface and crystallizing as water evaporates.

q: 23. King closers are related to .....
explain: King closers are special brick shapes used in brick masonry.

q: 24. The kiln which may work throughout the year, is .....
explain: Hoffman's kiln is a continuous kiln and can work throughout the year.

q: 25. Excess of silica in the clay .....
options: makers the brick brittle and weak
makes the brick crack and warp on drying
changes colour of the brick from red to yellow
improves impermeability and durability of the brick
explain: As per the answer key, excess silica makes the brick brittle and weak. (The book prints 'makers'.)

q: 26. Which of the following constituent, when present in excess quantity in clay causes the bricks to melt and distort during burning?
explain: As per the answer key, lime. Excess lime melts the clay in burning and distorts the bricks (alkalies also act as a flux, but the key gives c).

q: 27. The alkaline salt present in the bricks, absorbs moisture from the air which on drying .....
options: leaves pores and makes the bricks porous
leaves high powder deposit on the brick
makes the bricks brittle and weak
explain: As per the answer key, option b. Alkali salts absorb moisture and on drying leave a powdery deposit (efflorescence).

q: 28. The good clay for making bricks is .....
explain: Weathered clay is more plastic and uniform, so it is good for bricks.

q: 29. The process of mixing clay, water and other ingredients to make bricks, is known as .....
explain: As per the answer key, kneading. Note: other questions in the book use 'tempering' or 'pugging' for this operation.

q: 30. Percentage of silica in a good brick earth lies between
explain: Silica forms the bulk of good brick earth, typically comprising about 50 to 60%.

q: 31. The stretcher bond in brick masonry can be used only when the thickness of wall is
explain: Since stretcher bond shows only the long face of bricks, it is suitable only for half-brick-thick (9 cm) walls.

q: 32. Which of the following pairs gives a correct combination of the useful and harmful constituents respectively of a good brick earth?
explain: Silica is a useful (structural) constituent of brick earth, while alkalies are harmful, causing efflorescence.

q: 33. Number of brick required for one cubic meter of brick masonry is ( as per IS)
explain: As per this reference (IS), about 500 bricks are typically required per cubic meter of brick masonry.

q: 34. A queen closer is a
options: brick laid with its length parallel to the face or direction of wall
brick laid with its breadth parallel to the face or direction of wall
brick having the same length and depth as the other bricks but half the breadth
brick with half the width at one end and full width at the other
explain: A queen closer retains the full length and depth of a standard brick but has its breadth (width) halved.

q: 35. Minimum thickness of wall where single flemish bond can be used is
options: one and a half bricks thick
explain: Single Flemish bond requires a minimum wall thickness of one and a half bricks to properly interlock headers and stretchers.

q: 36. The most important tool in brick laying for lifting and spreading mortar and for forming joints is
explain: The trowel is the primary hand tool used by masons to lift, spread mortar, and finish joints.

q: 37. The slenderness ratio for masonry walls should not be more than
explain: For structural stability, the slenderness ratio of masonry walls is generally limited to a maximum of about 20.

q: 38. As compared to English bond, double flemish bond is
explain: Double Flemish bond requires more skilled labor and careful brick selection for its decorative pattern, making it costlier than English bond.

q: 39. Special material of construction capable of withstanding high temperature is:
explain: Refractory materials are specifically engineered to withstand very high temperatures without degrading.

q: 40. Hollow bricks are used for:
explain: The trapped air pockets in hollow bricks reduce heat transfer, providing thermal insulation.

q: 41. What should be the ratio of water absorption of a first class brick after 24 hours immersion?
explain: First class bricks should have a water absorption not exceeding about 20% of their weight after 24-hour immersion.

q: 42. The minimum compressive strength of first class bricks should be
explain: First class bricks are required to have a minimum compressive strength of about 10 N/mm2 as per this reference.

q: 43. A small quantity of magnesia in brick earth imparts
explain: A small amount of magnesia in brick earth is known to impart a yellowish tint to the fired brick.

q: 44. The good clay for making brick is
explain: Weathering breaks down the clay particles and removes impurities, making the clay more plastic and suitable for brick molding.
